    Service Standards

    The 10 Steps · LIFTS · the empowerment window.
    The 10 Steps of Service
    1. 60-second greet
      Eye contact + warm welcome. Cornell: +23% rating lift.
    2. $5.55 anchor pitch
      Food AND drinks. Eliminates price anxiety.
    3. The 3 R's
      Repeat · Read back · Right.
    4. Table to Terminal
      Order entered before any build.
    5. Drink delivery + scan
      Empty glass = lost revenue. Read the body language.
    6. Food + 2-bite check
      "How's everything taste so far?" Recovery window.
    7. Upsell at every stage
      Pitcher · Dumpster Dive · Add-ons. +10–15% revenue.
    8. Pre-bill check-in
      Last round? Dessert? Programming?
    9. Bill drop + verbal Google ask
      3–5× more reviews than QR alone.
    10. Memory Creating Moment
      Specific return invite tied to programming.
    LIFTS · Service Recovery
    L · Listen
    No interrupting. Full attention.
    I · Inform
    "Your food arrived cold — that's not what should've happened."
    F · Fix
    "I'm fixing that right now." Active, not passive.
    T · Thank
    "Thanks for letting us know instead of just leaving."
    S · Shift
    Escalate to MOD beyond your window.
    Empowerment Window
    Without ApprovalApology · Replace incorrect order · Re-fire cold food · Comp single item under $10 for clear service failure (once per table).
    Escalate to MOD Any comp above $10 · Bill adjustments · Emotional escalation · Safety · Overconsumption · Anything unsure.

    Operating Frameworks

    The three pillars behind every standard.
    The Synthesis

    Build systems specific enough to train anyone on. Lead in a way that makes people choose to be accountable. Deliver a guest experience so genuinely valuable it becomes the obvious choice in Edmonton.

    1 · The 30% Rule — Preston Lee
    CoreBuild systems first → Right people in them → Hold everyone accountable.
    Target COGS30%
    Target Labour30%
    Target Overhead30%
    Net Operating Profit10%
    2 · Alex Hormozi — $100M Offers / The Game
    Grand Slam OfferExperience so compelling guest focuses on gain, not spend. F&D has one — job is consistent delivery.
    Behaviour-First Accountability"Be accountable" is uncoachable. "Complete the table-touch log" is coachable.
    Person-Independent SystemsIf it only runs when one person is there, it's a job not a business.
    5-Reason CheckKnow what? Know how? Know why? Obstacle? Only the 5th — chose not to — is discipline.
    3 · HBR — Leadership & Accountability
    Chosen vs MandatedMandated → compliance, kills initiative. Chosen → ownership, above-and-beyond.
    The 50% LiftGenuine accountability culture = 50% higher chance of meeting performance.
    Manager ImpactSingle biggest influence on whether employees stay or leave.

    Setup & Help

    First-time setup · ongoing guidance · troubleshooting

    Welcome to Command Center

    This page walks you through everything: installing the app on your phone (do this first), first-time setup, daily use, and troubleshooting. The blue ? button (bottom-right) is always available for quick "How do I..?" questions on any page.

    Install first ↓
    ~2 min on your phone
    1First-Time Setup · Do This Once
    ⭐ Start here · Put the app on your phone (2 minutes)

    The Command Center is already live online, so you can install it on your phone right now. Open the app's web link (the one ownership texted/emailed you) on your phone, then follow your device below:

    📱 iPhone / iPad
    1. Open the link in Safari (not Chrome — Safari has the best app support on iOS)
    2. Tap the Share icon (the square with an up-arrow, bottom centre)
    3. Scroll down and tap "Add to Home Screen"
    4. Tap "Add" (top-right)
    5. The Five & Dive icon appears on your home screen — tap it to launch full-screen
    🤖 Android
    1. Open the link in Chrome
    2. Tap the ⋮ menu (top-right)
    3. Tap "Add to Home screen" (or "Install app")
    4. Confirm
    5. The icon appears on your home screen — tap it to launch full-screen
    Why install? Launching from the home-screen icon runs the app full-screen like a real app, keeps you signed in, and makes the 🎤 voice button and notifications work more reliably than a browser tab.
    First sign-in The first time you open it, pick your name and set your own password + recovery phrase. That's per-device, so do it on the phone you'll actually use on shift.
    Step 1 · Open the dashboard on your office computer
    1. Save the Five_Dive_Command_Center.html file to your computer (anywhere — Desktop is fine)
    2. Double-click to open in your web browser (Chrome recommended)
    3. The lock screen appears immediately
    Pro tip Right-click the file → "Open with" → pick Chrome to always use it. Then bookmark or pin the tab.
    Step 2 · Jerrod claims the master account FIRST

    Important: whoever signs in as "Jerrod Sutherland" first becomes the master. Do this before sharing the file with anyone.

    1. Pick "Jerrod Sutherland" from the dropdown
    2. Click Continue → it asks you to set a password (6+ chars)
    3. Pick a security question and answer it (case-insensitive)
    4. The dashboard generates a 4-word recovery phrase (e.g. cedar-thunder-violet-jasmine)
    5. SAVE THIS PHRASE NOW. Password manager, email it to yourself, write it down. You only see it once.
    6. Click "I've saved it" → you're signed in
    Critical If you lose both your password AND your security answer AND your recovery phrase, you cannot get back in. The phrase is your last-resort key.
    Step 3 · Take your first backup right now
    1. You should now see the Dashboard page
    2. Top-right, click "Backup"
    3. A JSON file downloads — name it something like five-dive-day-1-backup.json
    4. Email it to your personal Gmail OR drop into Google Drive / OneDrive / Dropbox
    Why now This is your safety net. If anything goes sideways during setup, you can Restore from this and you're back. Habit: backup every Sunday.
    Step 4 · Host the dashboard online (recommended for phone use)

    Right now you're running the dashboard from a local file. For phones — especially iPhone — hosting online is much more reliable. Pick one of these free options:

    Option A · Netlify Drop (easiest)
    1. Rename the file to index.html
    2. Go to app.netlify.com/drop
    3. Drag the file onto the page
    4. You get a URL like random-words-12345.netlify.app
    5. Sign up free to claim it; set a custom name like fivedive-command.netlify.app
    6. To update later: drag a new file onto the same site
    Option B · GitHub Pages (most professional)
    1. Sign up at github.com/signup (use work email)
    2. Top-right + → "New repository"
    3. Name it fivedive-command, set Public, check "Add README", create
    4. Click "Add file" → "Upload files" → drag the HTML file in → rename it to index.html → commit
    5. Repo settings → Pages → Source: "main" branch → Save
    6. Wait 1-2 min — your URL is https://YOURNAME.github.io/fivedive-command
    About privacy The URL is public but the lock screen protects all data. Anyone who finds the URL just sees a login screen.
    Try Netlify Try GitHub
    Step 5 · Get it on your phone

    Once hosted (Step 4), open the URL on your phone:

    📱 iPhone
    1. Open the URL in Safari (not Chrome — Safari has better PWA support on iOS)
    2. Tap the Share icon (square with up-arrow)
    3. Scroll and tap "Add to Home Screen"
    4. Tap "Add"
    5. Icon appears on your home screen — tap to launch full-screen
    🤖 Android
    1. Open the URL in Chrome
    2. Tap the ⋮ menu (top-right)
    3. Tap "Add to Home screen"
    4. Confirm
    5. Icon appears on your home screen — tap to launch
    First sign-in on phone Each device asks the user to set a password the first time. That's normal — passwords are per-device until you Backup → Restore between them.
    Step 6 · Distribute to your team
    1. Make sure you've already signed in as Jerrod (Step 2)
    2. Send each manager the URL via text or email
    3. Each manager:
      • Opens it on their phone (Step 5)
      • Picks their name from the dropdown
      • Sets their own password + recovery
      • Saves the recovery phrase
    4. If a manager isn't in the dropdown yet: Jerrod adds them via Settings → Manager Management

    Bitwarden · Operational Passwords
    Important Supplier passwords, social media, POS portals — those don't belong in this dashboard. They live in Bitwarden, a free password manager. Each manager signs up free, you share specific collections through an organization.
    Bitwarden setup steps
    1. Each manager: sign up free at bitwarden.com/signup with work email
    2. Each manager: install the iPhone/Android app + Chrome extension from bitwarden.com/download
    3. Jerrod: go to vault.bitwarden.com → "New organization" → name it "Five & Dive"
    4. For 3+ users, upgrade to Teams Starter (~$24/year for up to 10 users)
    5. Create collections: Suppliers, POS Portals, Social Media, Banking/Compliance
    6. Add each operational password to the right collection
    7. Invite each manager via their work email
    8. Assign which collections each role can see

    Troubleshooting
    "I lost data after updating to a new version"

    Starting with this version, the dashboard auto-migrates data forward. If you backup your data file (Settings → Backup) and Restore it, you're never going to lose anything.

    "I forgot my password"

    On the sign-in screen, tap "Forgot password?" — answer your security question OR paste your recovery phrase, set a new password. If both lost, Jerrod can reset you from Settings → Master Controls.

    "My phone keeps losing data after a few days"

    iPhone Safari clears local storage if you don't open the app for ~7 days. Fix: host the dashboard online (Section 1 → Step 4). Once it's a real website, iPhone gives it full storage permissions and data persists indefinitely.

    "The mic doesn't work / picks up wrong words"

    Browser needs mic permission (grant on first use). Loud bars = poor accuracy — use typed input below the mic button instead. Mic auto-stops after a pause; tap again to continue.

    "Someone's edits aren't showing up on my device"

    Each device has its own copy until someone Backups and shares the JSON for Restore. For real-time sync, the dashboard needs to move to a hosted backend (Path A) — separate project.

    "How do I add a new manager who isn't in the dropdown?"

    Only Jerrod can do this. Sign in as Jerrod → Settings → "Manager / Team Management" → fill in name/role → click + Add. The new manager then appears in the sign-in dropdown.

    Replaces: Existing shifts on any day covered by the email.
